summary: ALG (Alamo Group) is a -35.1% drawdown industrial machinery name where Form 4 evidence STRONGLY supports a LONG-tier verdict. New CEO Robert P. Hureau (joined Sept 2 2025) executed FIVE open-market code-P purchases totalling $250,831 in personal cash between Nov 13 2025 and Mar 9 2026, all at $161-$168 (~25% below the 2025 peak, i.e. INTO the drawdown). Director Nina Grooms added a $40K open-market buy Mar 24 2026. This is the canonical 'management commitment into drawdown' Form-4 pattern the prompt explicitly flags as LONG-tier evidence. Outgoing CEO Leonard sold $1.26M near the peak in May-Aug 2025 (pre-transition diversification, partially before the Aug 14 transition was announced), and EVP Veg-Mgmt Raborn sold $407K in May-June 2025 (now retiring per May 19 2026 8-K) — these are explainable as routine pre-separation behavior. The strongest Mode B finding (SEVERE) is that the 10-K trumpets Industrial Equipment as the bright spot but conceals that Industrial backlog fell -21% YoY in Q1 2026 with new orders -11% — the segment narrative is being held up by Ring-O-Matic + Petersen acquisitions while organic growth has flatlined. PASSes on auditor cleanliness (KPMG, no material weaknesses), legal proceedings, leverage (0.4x net post-Petersen), interest-rate hedging (swap through Aug 2027), Vegetation Mgmt restructuring credibility, and acquisition coherence. Verdict: LONG-tier. The Hureau open-market buying is the cleanest honesty-alpha LONG signal in this universe — a brand-new CEO with no contractual obligation to buy stock putting $250K cash in at depressed prices is high-conviction commitment, partially offset by one SEVERE Mode B on Industrial backlog (which Hureau himself presumably knows about).
